# Lullable

> Lullable is the low-arousal knowledge engine: an audio app that reads sleep stories and true, gently fascinating material in a warm, flat, progressively quieter voice, engineered so listeners fall asleep mid-sentence. It is the alternative to meditation apps for people whose racing minds cannot be emptied, only occupied. Not a medical device.

## Key pages
- [Home](https://getlullable.com/): what Lullable is, with an audio sample
- [The Sleep Library](https://getlullable.com/sleep/): essays on sleep and pleasantly uneventful knowledge
- [Stories](https://getlullable.com/stories/): every sleep story in the app
- [Chronotype quiz](https://getlullable.com/chronotype/): five questions, one of five sleep animals (blackbird to octopus)

- [What the app does](https://getlullable.com/app/): every feature question, answered in one sentence

## What Lullable does
- **What is Lullable?** Lullable is an iPhone app of long-form sleep stories for adults: 26 true, gently fascinating pieces — a Roman bathhouse at closing time, the life of a redwood, the rings of Saturn — read slowly and flatly by a named narrator, and engineered so you fall asleep partway through. It is not yet on the App Store.
- **Do the stories fade out on their own?** Yes. A sleep timer set to 15, 30, 45 or 60 minutes ends in a ten-second ramp down to silence rather than a hard stop. Every recording also ends that way on its own: the last thirty seconds of every story fade out. There is nothing to switch off.
- **Do I have to choose a story?** No. The first screen is Tonight, and it holds one story already chosen for you, with one Play button. No feed, no library to browse with a phone six inches from your face. The full library is there if you want it, but it is the second screen, not the first.
- **How long are the stories?** Between 20 and 41 minutes. Most run about 40 — long enough that you are not expected to reach the end, which is the point.
- **What are the stories about?** Four categories: Ancient Worlds, Cosmic Journeys, Gentle Nature and Cozy Tales. All of it is true material rather than fiction, told in order, with the ending given away in the first line so there is never a reason to stay awake for it.
- **Are there ads?** No. Lullable has no advertising in it, and no version of this business has one — a mid-roll at 3am wakes the person it is sold to.
- **Does it keep playing when the screen locks?** Yes. Background and lock-screen playback, with the transport on the lock screen. Put the phone face down and leave it.
- **Where does it start again the next night?** A minute before you lost the thread — not at the point the audio stopped, which is always later than the point you stopped hearing it.
- **Is there a streak, a score or a sleep graph?** None of the three. The morning screen shows the last line you heard and the time you stopped listening. That is all it knows and all it claims. There is no number to improve on and nothing to keep up.
- **Who reads the stories?** Named narrators, in male and female voices — Emma from Oxford, Amy from Greenwich, Arthur from Ludlow, Brian from St Ives, Niamh from Kinsale, Patrick from Block Island. Every one reads flat and warm, removing emphasis rather than adding it, and gets quieter across the episode.
- **What does it cost?** Free to download, with one story — Aristotle, the Greatest Philosopher, 40 minutes — free to listen to in full. The subscription price is not announced until the App Store listing resolves; we would rather say nothing than quote a figure that moves.
- **Is there an Android version?** Not yet. iPhone only.
- **Is Lullable a medical device or a treatment for insomnia?** No, and it does not claim to be. It is audio designed for people whose minds will not stand down at night. If you have clinical insomnia, see a doctor.

## Essays
- [Marine snow: the slowest weather on Earth](https://getlullable.com/sleep/marine-snow/): A perpetual fall of debris from the sunlit ocean toward the floor — weeks in transit, arriving as ooze that deepens by centimetres per thousand years.
- [Boring voices to fall asleep to, and what makes one work](https://getlullable.com/sleep/boring-voices-to-fall-asleep-to/): The narrator qualities nobody writes about: narrow pitch, even pace, no performance. What the acoustics research says a voice has to stop doing.
- [Sleep stories without ads, and why a mid-roll at 3am is the whole problem](https://getlullable.com/sleep/sleep-stories-without-ads/): Almost everything written for this search is a children's app. Why an ad at 3am is structural rather than annoying, and what paying actually buys.
- [The shipping forecast at 00:48](https://getlullable.com/sleep/the-shipping-forecast-at-0048/): Thirty-one sea areas, read in the same clockwise order every night on Radio 4, inside a 380-word limit. An account of radio's quietest ritual.
- [Sleep stories for adults who overthink](https://getlullable.com/sleep/sleep-stories-for-adults-who-overthink/): An overthinking mind turns anything it is given into a task, including sleep. What a story has to withhold to survive that, and what to look for.
- [What to think about to fall asleep](https://getlullable.com/sleep/what-to-think-about-to-fall-asleep/): You can't think about nothing. The answer isn't a way to stop thought — it's a subject to hand it: true, concrete, flat, and going nowhere.
- [The best boring history podcasts to fall asleep to](https://getlullable.com/sleep/boring-history-podcast-to-fall-asleep-to/): An honest guide to the boring-history sleep genre — Sleep With Me, Nothing Much Happens, Sleepy History — and how the shows actually differ.
- [Why do I wake up at 3am with my mind racing?](https://getlullable.com/sleep/waking-up-at-3am-mind-racing/): Waking at 3am is normal — sleep is cyclical and cortisol is already climbing. Why the racing arrives, and why reaching for your phone backfires.
- [The cognitive shuffle: the sleep trick for overthinkers](https://getlullable.com/sleep/cognitive-shuffle-method/): Imagine a series of random, unrelated things until your thinking stops making sense. The technique, the research behind it, and how to do it tonight.
- [The width of a horse: how the railway gauge was chosen](https://getlullable.com/sleep/the-standard-railway-gauge/): Most of the world's trains run 4 feet 8½ inches apart. Nobody chose that number. It was inherited from colliery carts and ratified long after it had won.
- [Why do podcasts keep me awake when I'm exhausted?](https://getlullable.com/sleep/why-do-podcasts-keep-me-awake/): Podcasts are engineered to hold attention — hooks, cliffhangers, autoplay. Why that beats your exhaustion, and what kind of audio works instead.
- [How long should it take to fall asleep?](https://getlullable.com/sleep/how-long-does-it-take-to-fall-asleep/): Ten to twenty minutes is the healthy normal — and falling asleep instantly isn't the goal. What sleep latency is, and when it's worth attention.
- [The weather at the bottom of the sea](https://getlullable.com/sleep/the-weather-at-the-bottom-of-the-sea/): There is weather at the bottom of the Mariana Trench — currents, storms of sediment, warm springs. A quiet tour of the calmest climate on Earth.
- [Two men on Ben Nevis, every hour, for 21 years](https://getlullable.com/sleep/two-men-on-ben-nevis/): From 1883 to 1904, observers on Britain's highest summit took a weather reading every single hour. A story about patience, fog, and 1.5 million numbers.
- [What are sleep stories, and do they work?](https://getlullable.com/sleep/what-are-sleep-stories/): Sleep stories are audio narratives built to be abandoned mid-listen. How they work, when they beat meditation and white noise, and what to look for.
- [What is low-arousal learning?](https://getlullable.com/sleep/what-is-low-arousal-learning/): Audio engineered to sit just below the threshold of engagement — fascinating enough to hold a racing mind, calm enough to release it into sleep.
- [Why can't I stop thinking at night?](https://getlullable.com/sleep/why-cant-i-stop-thinking-at-night/): A racing mind at bedtime usually isn't insomnia — it's an unoccupied brain. Why silence backfires for overthinkers, and what actually works.

## Stories
- [The Midnight Museum Beneath the Sea](https://getlullable.com/stories/the-midnight-museum-beneath-the-sea/): 20-minute gentle nature sleep story. The ocean arranged as a museum with its light on floors: gold at the foyer, cathedral blue in the middle, and a midnight gallery that lights itself.
- [The Midnight Sleeper Train Across the Alps](https://getlullable.com/stories/the-midnight-sleeper-train-across-the-alps/): 40-minute cozy tales sleep story. Board the midnight-blue sleeper in Vienna, hand over your passport, and let the train do the rest while borders pass over you like weather.
- [The Slow Life of a Redwood](https://getlullable.com/stories/the-slow-life-of-a-redwood/): 41-minute gentle nature sleep story. A coastal grove at dusk, a tree older than the cathedrals, and one unbroken thread of water travelling from the roots to the highest needle.
- [Floating Through the Pillars of Creation](https://getlullable.com/stories/floating-through-the-pillars-of-creation/): 41-minute cosmic journeys sleep story. You rise from your own roof and keep going, past every planet, until the stars thicken into a cloud with three dark columns standing in the middle of it.
- [A Roman Bathhouse at Closing Time](https://getlullable.com/stories/a-roman-bathhouse-at-closing-time/): 39-minute ancient worlds sleep story. A provincial bathhouse at the gentlest hour of its day: the crowd gone home, the lamps being lit, and a floor warmed by a fire nobody sees.
- [Aristotle, the Greatest Philosopher](https://getlullable.com/stories/aristotle-the-greatest-philosopher/): 40-minute ancient worlds sleep story. A boy on a Greek shore who never stopped asking what is this, and the twenty-three centuries of patient looking that followed.
